name: Codeine
label: Sub Pop
lede: Three Oberlin kids who played so slowly that Sub Pop asked for more grunge guitar, said no, and wrote the rulebook for slowcore in three records.

eras.title: Oberlin, a $98 bass, and a vision of slowness
eras.text: Codeine grew out of Oberlin College friendships and a New York couch. Stephen Immerwahr had an idea for music that barely moved, and found two people patient enough to play it.

years.h: Stephen Immerwahr arrives at Oberlin with a $98 Vox bass
years.p: Immerwahr's Vox Beatle bass would carry Codeine. At Oberlin he overlapped with [[Chris Brokaw|a05544f2-9341-4c9d-8ba0-7621a23012c6]], [[Sooyoung Park|403de443-6062-4f06-bd45-be02974a9441]] of [[Bitch Magnet|6be97715-b3fe-421b-b478-c4462ee9de15]], [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] and [[Liz Phair|149326c2-b8a3-48e3-b3d2-9b5b9593127f]].

years.h: Stephen Immerwahr meets John Engle, couch-surfing in New York
years.p: [[John Engle|b6261573-22eb-4d89-9f67-feb11b3ac92d]], whose brother was an Oberlin alum, was crashing in New York. Immerwahr says he knew on meeting him that he wanted a band with him.

years.h: Codeine takes shape: music that moves by very slowly
years.p: After a project called Squid with drummer Peter Pollack, Immerwahr and Engle add Oberlin grad Chris Brokaw, son of a bebop drummer, on drums.
years.xp: Immerwahr had been working as an assistant engineer since 1988, on sessions for bands like [[Soul Asylum|b10db9ad-b4c3-47f3-a7a4-37864b134f65]] and Living Colour. He later said he was after the slowness of depressive states and opiate states, and the intensity that comes from playing slow on purpose.

years.h: First show: the Middle East, opening for Bitch Magnet
years.p: Codeine debut at the Cambridge club under Bitch Magnet and Green Magnet School. [[Doug Scharin|979a7fb2-872d-454d-8c01-96cfed8a53d9]], their future drummer, is in the crowd.

eras.title: A dirt floor and a grunge label
eras.text: Codeine made its debut in a basement for almost nothing, put it out in Germany first, and then found itself on the hottest label in America, which wanted it to sound more like everyone else on the label.

years.h: Frigid Stars gets cut in Mike McMackin's basement
years.p: Dirt floor, an eight-track, a dehumidifier between takes, overdubs in the boiler room. [[Mike McMackin|6b450a4a-56ed-4745-8d3e-fcc9f0247ee9]] says they had no budget to speak of.

years.h: Frigid Stars LP comes out in Europe on Glitterhouse
years.p: Germany's Glitterhouse issues it after the Pickup Song 7-inch. The sleeve title comes from a line by [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]]; Melody Maker called the record astonishing and profoundly moving.
years.xp: Immerwahr researched star imagery at the New York Public Library for the sleeve. The back cover is John Engle's photo of a friend on a mattress in an Avenue A apartment.

years.h: Sub Pop signs Codeine, then asks for Jack Endino guitars
years.p: Jonathan Poneman and Bruce Pavitt saw Codeine's fifth show at TT the Bear's in Cambridge and signed them. Then Poneman asked if they'd fly to Seattle to add fuzz with [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]]. They declined.
years.xp:
Sub Pop's US edition in May 1991 added 3 Angels and a distorted-guitar version of Pea, but the album stayed as the band made it.

Immerwahr later noted the deal gave Sub Pop the records in perpetuity. The upside: they never went out of print.

years.h: Opening for Smashing Pumpkins, Unrest and the Jesus Lizard
years.p: Codeine plays under [[Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]] and [[Unrest|f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c]], and opens for [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] in Boston to a crowd puzzled by the Sub Pop deal. That fall they tour Europe with [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]]' band [[Bastro|cfc5b1bf-a46c-4504-bcb6-a820416a1894]].

years.h: Chris Brokaw's other band, Come, puts out Car on Sub Pop
years.p: Brokaw has switched to guitar with [[Thalia Zedek|a22a05de-b2e2-437c-91fc-df7b67ceb584]] in Come. John Engle could already tell Brokaw wouldn't stay in Codeine.

eras.title: The year every session went wrong
eras.text: Codeine spent 1992 in studios across New York and Boston and hated most of what came out. An album got shelved, the drummer left, and the band survived on a 25-minute EP.

q: I thought it was the best thing we'd done.
years.p: Codeine recorded a second album at Harold Dessau Recording in Manhattan with Mike McMackin, then scrapped it. Stephen Immerwahr didn't want it to be their last word.
years.xp: Immerwahr later said all their 1992 recordings went terribly. The songs, including Sea, Tom and Wird, were re-recorded later with a new drummer.

years.h: Chris Brokaw leaves for Come; Doug Scharin of Rex joins
years.p: Josh Madell of Antietam fills in on a US tour, then Doug Scharin, who'd seen Codeine's first Boston show, takes over drums.

years.h: Barely Real: a 25-minute EP from a bad year
years.p: Pieced together from sessions at Toxic Shock and Harold Dessau in New York and a Boston studio. David Grubbs arranges the piano piece W.; Melody Maker called it 25 minutes of snowblind glory.

eras.title: The White Birch and the long way home
eras.text: With Doug Scharin, Codeine made its most ambitious record in three studios, toured Europe until it hurt, and then simply stopped because the songs had.

years.h: The White Birch: the one Low and Mogwai learned from
years.p: Recorded in 1993 in Chicago, Middletown, Connecticut, and New York, with David Grubbs on guitar for Tom and Wird. Spin gave it 9 out of 10.
years.xp: Clean guitars break into heavy distortion, a step away from the bare early sound. Select compared it to monks doing plainsong remixes.

years.h: A long European tour, then Codeine stops
years.p: Immerwahr says the band ended because there stopped being new songs, plus interpersonal stuff. He and John Engle took jobs at the Department of Health and in market research.
years.xp: Immerwahr later left music for a career as a research scientist and formed Raymond. Doug Scharin went on to Rex, [[June of 44|56f3de75-2c88-4054-a1df-65c661f4ee0f]] and HiM.

eras.title: Numero calls
eras.text: A reissue box brought the original trio back for a handful of shows. The hard part, they found, was playing that slow again.

years.h: First reunion show: I'll Be Your Mirror at Alexandra Palace
years.p: Stephen Immerwahr, John Engle and Chris Brokaw play London; the run ends July 15 at Le Poisson Rouge in New York. Engle says the first seven or eight rehearsals went nowhere.

years.h: Numero Group reissues everything in When I See the Sun
years.p: The box collects Frigid Stars, Barely Real and The White Birch with rarities, including four songs from the shelved Dessau session.

eras.title: The lost album and the last shows
eras.text: Thirty years late, the record Codeine threw away came out, and the band played what it said would be its final shows, then a few more abroad in 2024.

years.p: Numero Group releases the eight songs from Harold Dessau Recording. NPR's Sarah Hennies said it felt like a ghost in her living room.

q: The shows we play this year will be our last.
years.h: Union Pool, Brooklyn: Codeine's first show in 11 years
years.p: A week later they play the Numero Group's 20th anniversary festival in Los Angeles. Despite the farewell talk, shows in Canada, Australia, Japan and Mexico follow in 2024.
years.xp: Immerwahr showed up in black metal T-shirts; Brokaw had recorded an acoustic version of a Vlad Tepes song.

years.h: Codeine plays Atmosphere for Low's Mimi Parker
years.p: Codeine dedicates its Joy Division cover to [[Low|42faad37-8aaa-42e4-a300-5a7dae79ed24]]'s [[Mimi Parker|31e0783a-9c5d-4218-9f23-4b9427b111e7]], who died in November 2022. The two bands had shared a Joy Division tribute album in the '90s.
